commitments.target: FY27 credit cost guidance of 4% to 4.5%
commitments.quote: Our FY27 credit cost guidance of 4% to 4.5% reflects a new PAR 15 accretion rate of 30-35 bps per month.
commitments.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan

commitments.target: Medium-term foreign borrowings target of 25-30% by FY28
commitments.quote: Our foreign borrowings stood healthy at 24.3%, moving closer to the medium-term target of 25-30% by FY28 as we scale our business.
commitments.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan

claims.claim: X bucket collection efficiency stood at 99.71% in December 2025.
claims.quote: Our X bucket collection efficiency stood at 99.71% in December 2025, while monthly PAR 15+ accretion declined sharply to 18 bps in December 2025 from 47 bps in September 2025.

claims.claim: Q3 FY26 disbursements grew 13.4% YoY to INR 5,767 Crore.
claims.quote: The disbursements for Q3 FY26 stood at INR 5,767 Crore, increasing by 13.4% YoY with the exit month December crossing INR 2,200 Crore mark.

claims.claim: Average cost of borrowings declined 26 bps QoQ to 9.4%.
claims.quote: Our average cost of borrowings continues to trend lower, reflecting disciplined liability management, having declined 26 bps QoQ to 9.4% at the end of Q3 FY26.

claims.claim: Net interest income grew 13.4% YoY to INR 977 Crore.
claims.quote: Net interest income grew 13.4% YoY to INR 977 Crore with portfolio yield of 21.0% versus 20.7% in Q2 FY26.

claims.claim: PAT doubled QoQ to INR 252 Crore in Q3 FY26.
claims.quote: PAT doubled QoQ to INR 252 Crore, while adjusted figures stood at INR 266 Crore, translating to an ROA and ROE of 3.5% and 13.8%, respectively.

claims.claim: NIM increased by 60 bps QoQ to 13.9% in Q3 FY26.
claims.quote: NIM increased by 60 bps QoQ to 13.9% in Q3 FY26.

analyst_concerns.question: What is the asset quality trend in UP, Bihar, and Madhya Pradesh?
analyst_concerns.quote: Can some colour about trends in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh compared to the April-24 number that you had given us last year, they are still probably 15 to 20 bps higher currently? So, what is the trend over there?

analyst_concerns.question: How is Karnataka seeing recovery when other non-MFI lenders report disturbed credit discipline?
analyst_concerns.quote: While you guys have reported great numbers, some of the non-MFI lenders commentary earlier this quarter or maybe even closer to December was that the credit discipline in Karnataka state, which got disturbed after the MFI ordinance came into place, which impacted our retail loans also is still not back.

analyst_concerns.question: Are bank lines drying up or becoming more expensive for NBFC-MFIs?
analyst_concerns.quote: Even if the lines are available, they are coming at a significantly higher cost of funds. So, if you can speak to us about the -- any challenges or any areas that we are struggling with our bank borrowings or our bank relationships.

analyst_concerns.question: How have rejection rates trended after the implementation of MFIN guardrails?
analyst_concerns.quote: Sir, first thing on the industry, most other players talk about a very high rejection rate today, especially after the implementation of MFIN guardrails. So, if you could just help us understand how have our rejection rates trended over the last maybe 2, 3 quarters?
